tour.name: Yogyakarta Private Tour: Borobudur at Sunrise, Prambanan & the Sultan's Palace
tour.subtitle: A private day in the cultural capital of Java with a licensed guide and car: sunrise over the volcanoes from the Setumbu hill, the Buddhist monument of Borobudur, a village lunch, the Hindu temples of Prambanan and the Kraton palace of the Sultan of Yogyakarta.

tour.overview:
In the 8th and 9th centuries, the kingdoms of central Java built two of the greatest religious monuments in Asia: Borobudur, a Buddhist stupa in the form of a mountain with nine stacked terraces, and, a few decades later, Prambanan, a cluster of Hindu temples whose central tower rises 47 metres. Both were abandoned and buried under volcanic ash and jungle for centuries, then restored in the 20th century. Both are UNESCO World Heritage Sites, inscribed in 1991. Nearby, Yogyakarta is still ruled by a sultan and remains the centre of Javanese culture.

This private day shows the great monuments and the living culture of Yogyakarta with a licensed guide and a car. You watch the sunrise over Borobudur and the volcanoes, explore the monument and its reliefs, visit the small temple of Mendut, have lunch in a village, see Prambanan and end at the Sultan's palace.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 12 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Yogyakarta
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; steps at the sunrise point and at the temples

WHAT YOU SEE
• Sunrise from Setumbu hill.
• Borobudur.
• Mendut temple.
• Prambanan.
• The Kraton of Yogyakarta.

WHY THIS WORKS
We see Borobudur in the cool of the morning and Prambanan in the afternoon, with a relaxed lunch in between, and end in town at the palace.

WHO IT SUITS
History and culture lovers, photographers and anyone travelling through Java or visiting from Bali.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want volcanoes, ask us about Mount Bromo and the Ijen crater in East Java.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
To protect the monument, climbing Borobudur's upper terraces is limited to small timed groups with authorised guides and special sandals; we book it when available, otherwise you walk around the base and the lower galleries. Yogyakarta is about one hour by plane from Bali.

days.name: Sunrise at Setumbu, Borobudur, Mendut, a village lunch, Prambanan and the Sultan's Kraton
days.description:
What to expect: the two great temple complexes of central Java and the Sultan's palace, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 3:30 and drive north-west, about an hour, to Setumbu hill. A short climb by torchlight brings you to a viewpoint where, as the sun rises, the stupa of Borobudur emerges from the mist in the valley, with the volcanoes Merapi and Merbabu behind.

You enter Borobudur as it opens. Built around 800 by the Sailendra dynasty, it is a stepped pyramid of about two million volcanic stones, built without mortar on a hill. Pilgrims walked clockwise around each terrace, reading the story of the Buddha in 2,672 carved panels, from the world of desire at the bottom to the world of form, and up to the formless world of the round upper terraces, where 72 perforated stupas each hold a seated Buddha. When available, you join an authorised small group to climb to the summit wearing special sandals that protect the stones; otherwise your guide reads the reliefs with you around the base and the lower galleries. You also visit Mendut, a small temple whose chamber holds a 3-metre seated Buddha flanked by two bodhisattvas, in perfect condition after twelve centuries.

Lunch is in a village among the rice fields, with Javanese dishes such as gudeg, young jackfruit stewed in palm sugar and coconut milk. In the afternoon you visit Prambanan, built in the 9th century for the Hindu trinity: the central temple of Shiva, 47 metres tall, flanked by the temples of Vishnu and Brahma, decorated with reliefs of the Ramayana. You end in Yogyakarta at the Kraton, the palace of the Sultan, still his residence, with its pavilions, gamelan orchestras and royal servants in traditional dress. You are back at your hotel at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
03:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
04:45 – Setumbu hill for sunrise.
06:30 – Borobudur (about 2 hours 30 minutes).
09:15 – Mendut temple.
11:00 – Village lunch.
13:00 – Prambanan.
15:00 – The Sultan's Kraton.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Kraton is open in the morning only on some days; we adapt the order.
• The Ramayana ballet is performed at Prambanan on many evenings and can be added.
• A batik or silver workshop in Kotagede can be visited on request.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, sunrise entrance, temple and palace tickets, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Ramayana ballet, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we climb Borobudur?
faq.answer: Climbing to the upper terraces is limited to small timed groups with authorised guides. We book it when available; otherwise you explore the base and lower levels with your guide.

faq.question: Can we come from Bali?
faq.answer: Yes. Yogyakarta is about an hour's flight from Bali. We can arrange the flight and a night in Yogyakarta.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the sunrise viewpoint, Borobudur, Mendut, Prambanan and the Kraton.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, Javanese dishes in a village. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who manage an early start. They enjoy the stories carved in stone. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The temple grounds have paved paths, but the sunrise hill and the monuments have steep steps.

faq.question: What is the dress code?
faq.answer: Covered shoulders and knees at the temples and the palace; a sarong may be provided.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops at batik or silver workshops unless you ask.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Indonesia but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light covering clothes, comfortable shoes, a light jacket for the early morning and a hat.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May to October is dry. In the rainy season, mornings are usually clear and sunrises can be spectacular.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
